case_title: Sharanjit Kaur & Anr. v. State of Punjab
accused_occupation: Described by the Court as 'agents' who dupe people (no formal occupation stated)
accused_victim_relationship: Transactional only: complainant paid accused in instalments for a promised job abroad for his son; no personal relationship described
evidence_type: Documentary as alleged: complainant's affidavit and dishonoured cheque (not adjudicated by the Court)
aggravating_circumstances: Serious allegations of fraud; alleged duping of Rs. 30 lakh; Court noted practice of duping innocent and rustic villagers
trial_court_outcome: Not stated; no trial described. Additional Sessions Judge dismissed anticipatory bail applications
high_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail petitions and Criminal Writ Petition No. 1843 of 2012 dismissed
neutral_facts: The complainant alleged that the accused took about Rs 30 lakh in several instalments from him on the pretext of arranging a permanent job abroad for his son. The promised job was not secured and the promise was not honoured. The accused then issued a cheque for Rs 30 lakh to the complainant, dated 23 February 2012, which was dishonoured for insufficient funds. The complainant alleged that he sold his property and arranged funds to make the payments. On 3 April 2012 the complainant lodged a first information report alleging cheating under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code against four persons, including the accused. The complainant filed an affidavit setting out these details, and the dishonoured cheque is part of the record. The State contended that the accused repeatedly failed to join enquiry proceedings called by a village panchayat. The State also contended that criminal courts have no bar on proceedings against the accused and that the police may investigate the offence. The legal question concerned whether a Gram Panchayat, rather than the police and regular criminal courts, could deal with an offence of this kind.
number_of_offences: 1 charged (IPC s.420, as stated in FIR); 0 finally upheld (no conviction; appeals against anticipatory bail refusal dismissed)
financial_property_loss: Rs. 30 lakh alleged paid to accused; cheque of Rs. 30 lakh dishonoured
motive: alleged: financial gain by promising a permanent job abroad for the complainant's son
key_evidence_accepted: No evidence weighed on merits; Court relied on the serious nature of the FIR allegations of Rs. 30 lakh fraud to hold the offence should be tried by a regular criminal court
post_offence_conduct: As alleged by the State: accused did not join panchayat enquiry despite repeated calls (not adjudicated)
bail_history: Anticipatory bail refused by Additional Sessions Judge (19.04.2012; 18.05.2012) and High Court (03.05.2012; 23.07.2012). Supreme Court stayed arrest of co-accused on 21.09.2012. Interim protection vacated on dismissal
trial_duration: offence: not given (FIR lodged 03.04.2012); trial judgment: not given; High Court: 23.07.2012 and 07.11.2012; Supreme Court: 01.07.2013
legal_representation: Accused: R.K. Kapoor. State: Ajay Kapur, AAG (amicus: A.S. Chandhiok, ASG)
investigation_status: FIR No. 17 registered 03.04.2012; investigation to be conducted by police; no charge sheet mentioned
appeal_history: Trial court: not applicable (anticipatory bail refused by Additional Sessions Judge). High Court: anticipatory bail and writ petition dismissed. Supreme Court: appeals dismissed
prosecution_argument: Serious cheating allegations; criminal courts have no bar on proceedings; police may investigate; Gram Panchayat has no jurisdiction over this offence
defence_argument: Punjab Panchayati Raj Act gives Gram Panchayat jurisdiction over the offence, so IPC proceedings are unsustainable and no police investigation can be carried out
legal_principle_applied: Police power to investigate and arrest is not abridged; Gram Panchayat has no jurisdiction until investigation is complete; transfer under s.45 needed; serious s.420 offence to be tried by regular criminal court
precedent_relied_upon: Chhotey Lal v. State, AIR 1967 All 229; Bhim Sen v. State of U.P., AIR 1955 SC 435; State of M.P. v. Shobharam, AIR 1966 SC 1910; Meena Ram v. Master Dwarki, AIR 1958 Punjab 417 (held inapplicable); Giani Ram v. Attar Chand, AIR 1960 Punjab 80; Baldeo Singh v. State of Bihar, AIR 1957 SC 612; Kartar Singh v. Pritam Singh, AIR 1956 Pepsu 78 (referred to)
judicial_aggravating_factors: Seriousness of the cheating allegations and alleged Rs. 30 lakh loss to the complainant
other_sentence_order: Interim protection vacated; investigation to be conducted by police
